Record date: 2130-02-08
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 02/08/30 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Worsening shortness of breath and increased sputum production since last visit.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit two days after the initiation of Meropenem therapy. The patient reports a slight increase in overall respiratory distress, characterized by more pronounced shortness of breath, especially during minimal exertion. He describes the sputum as remaining thick and yellow-green, with an increased volume noted over the past 48 hours. Despite adherence to his nebulizer regimen, he reports that the relief from wheezing and dyspnea has been fleeting.
Mr. Fairfax continues to experience intermittent low-grade fevers, which have not improved since the last visit, and he expresses concern regarding the persistence of his symptoms. He denies any chest pain but notes an increase in fatigue, which he attributes to both respiratory distress and anxiety about his condition.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, - night sweats, - chills, + intermittent low-grade fever. Pulmonary - + productive cough with thick yellow-green sputum, + dyspnea, + wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, - orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - + mild epigastric discomfort, - stable heartburn, - nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - no joint pain. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 130/82 mmHg - Heart Rate: 92 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 30 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 75% on supplemental oxygen (25 L via nasal cannula).
General: The patient appears more fatigued than during the last visit and is in significant respiratory distress, requiring assistance with positioning.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Severe wheezing and prolonged expiration noted on auscultation; bilateral diminished breath sounds; rhonchi and crackles are more pronounced, particularly in the lower lung fields.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender; mild epigastric discomfort persists; no hepatosplenomegaly.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation with ongoing bacterial infection, likely persistent Pseudomonas aeruginosa; sputum characteristics remain concerning for inadequate response to Meropenem. 2. Significant respiratory distress with inadequate improvement despite antibiotic therapy; thickening of sputum suggests ongoing bronchial obstruction or persistent infection. 3. Persistent fatigue and anxiety affecting quality of life; gastrointestinal symptoms remain stable.
PLAN
1. Continue Meropenem 1 g IV every 8 hours, given lack of clinical improvement; consider obtaining sputum culture and sensitivity to tailor antibiotic therapy more effectively. 2. Increase Prednisone to 80 mg daily to manage inflammation, with a tapering plan contingent upon clinical response; continue Omeprazole at 40 mg daily to mitigate gastrointestinal side effects. 3. Increase supplemental oxygen to 30 L via nasal cannula; monitor for signs of respiratory failure or hypoxemia closely. 4. Schedule a repeat chest X-ray to evaluate for any new complications, such as pneumonia or pleural effusion; bronchoscopy remains an option for further evaluation if no significant improvement is noted. 5. Continue nebulized bronchodilator therapy (Albuterol) every four hours as needed, and maintain Ipratropium bromide therapy; consider adding a mucolytic agent to assist with sputum clearance. 6. Schedule follow-up visit in 48 hours to reassess respiratory function, sputum characteristics, and overall clinical condition; consider referral to pulmonology if no significant improvement is observed.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax will remain under close observation in the internal medicine unit. The treatment team will continue to monitor his clinical status, particularly focusing on respiratory function and infection management. Patient education will be reinforced regarding the importance of adherence to the treatment regimen and the need to report any new or worsening symptoms, particularly related to respiratory function or changes in sputum production.
